Wednesday 04 November 2026 · 23 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 1.58% to 23,811 on narrow participation
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +6.00% weighted by turnover, against +0.24% for the median stock, a gap of 5.8 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Nelcast Limited rose 14.2% on 95 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Link of Recording”.

ITI Limited rose 1.1% on 162 times its usual volume. NSE asked the company to explain the move, “Significant increase in volume has been observed in ITI Limited. The Exchange, in order to ensure that investors have latest relevant information about the company and…”.

Trident Limited rose 7.1% on 104 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about capacity or expansion, “Capacity Expansion and Modernization Project”.

The exchange has formally asked 1 company to explain today's move: ITI Limited. Those queries were filed after the close, so they confirm the move rather than explain it. NSE's own surveillance flagged the same names.

What happened
Breaking
RBI launches 3 surveys to capture inflation expectations, consumer confidence ahead of December policy meeting
The Reserve Bank of India launched its bi-monthly surveys covering household inflation expectations and urban consumer confidence across 19 cities ahead of the December policy meeting. Quantified household inflation perceptions directly influence the Monetary Policy Committee's real rate assumptions and the interest rate trajectory. Shifts in these consumer sentiment metrics affect valuation multiples across rate-sensitive sectors, primarily retail banking, auto, and real estate.
ET Economy · +1 other
Sebi levies Rs 40 lakh penalty on four entities in Axis MF front-running case
SEBI penalized four entities a total of Rs 40 lakh for front-running Axis Mutual Fund trades between April 2021 and March 2022. This regulatory order concludes legacy enforcement actions without systemic impact on fund flows or earnings for parent Axis Bank. It reinforces compliance oversight on institutional brokerages without altering asset management sector valuations or market liquidity.
ET Markets · +1 other
Buy Birla Corporation; target of Rs 1100: Motilal Oswal
Single-broker rating revisions for Birla Corporation carry no broader market or sector impact without fresh corporate filings.

Textile, garment stocks in demand; Kitex, Trident, Gokaldas rally up to 18%
Kitex Garments rose 18% and Trident gained 13% on heavy trading volume driven by shifts in global garment sourcing. Export-oriented Indian textile manufacturers benefit when supply chain disruptions in Bangladesh divert North American apparel orders to domestic exporters. Order book growth and export realization figures in upcoming quarterly filings will confirm whether these volume surges reflect durable revenue expansion.

Your themes
Waaree doubles Texas solar module manufacturing capacity to 3.2 GW - pv magazine Global
Waaree Energies expanded its solar module manufacturing plant in Texas to 3.2 GW, doubling its operational capacity in the United States. Local manufacturing allows the company to qualify for Inflation Reduction Act tax incentives while bypassing potential US import tariffs on Asian solar components. Higher domestic production capability protects export operating margins and secures dollar-denominated revenue for the listed parent company.

US stocks today: Nasdaq rebounds as chipmakers rally, Apple slides ahead of US midterm results
The Nasdaq rebounded on semiconductor gains while Apple fell over rising component costs, reflecting divergent technology sector margin expectations. Global semiconductor shifts influence sentiment in Indian electronics manufacturing services companies, though overnight US equity movements primarily affect India through foreign portfolio flows and rupee volatility. Consistent foreign institutional investment data over the next two sessions will signal if broader US sentiment triggers domestic capital inflows.

Waaree Expands US Solar Manufacturing Capacity To 4.8 GW Amid Data Centre Demand - TradingView
Waaree Energies commissioned an expanded 4.8 GW solar module plant in Texas to supply power-hungry US data centres. The US expansion targets IRA tax incentives and higher module realisations than domestic sales, lifting overall export margins for the listed parent. Order backlogs and shipment guidance in the upcoming quarterly filing will confirm US execution speed.

Indian gold demand down 30% in September quarter as high prices hurt jewellery sales
Indian gold demand fell 30% year-on-year in the September quarter as record prices choked retail jewellery volumes and encouraged smuggling. The volume decline squeezes same-store sales growth for listed jewellers like Titan and Kalyan Jewellers, though higher realisations soften revenue impact. October-November festive sales figures will reveal whether lower import duties successfully revive festival buying.

Markets extend gains for fourth day; FPI buying highest in a year
Foreign portfolio investors recorded their largest single-day net equity purchase in a year, pushing the Nifty up 1.6% over four sessions. Reversing months of persistent selling, these inflows support rupee stability and expand valuation multiples across index heavyweights in banking and IT. Fortnightly NSDL FPI flow disclosures will confirm whether this foreign buying represents structural re-allocation.
BS Markets · +1 other
Morning Bid: Markets await midterms
Global markets paused ahead of US election results, which dictate dollar strength, US Treasury yields, and emerging market portfolio flows. Any yield surge strengthens the US dollar index, pressuring the rupee and triggering net foreign outflows from Indian equities. Weekly US Treasury auction yields and the US Dollar Index will indicate foreign flow directions into India.
Reuters Business
Market volatility healthy as money rotates out of AI, says analyst
Global funds are reallocating capital out of high-valuation US artificial intelligence equities into cyclical and value assets. This global portfolio rebalancing improves foreign portfolio flows into Indian equities, particularly capital goods and private banks trading at reasonable valuations. Continued net foreign inflows into Indian cash markets over the coming sessions will confirm whether this capital rotation reaches domestic equities.
Reuters Business
Macro and economy
Brokerages favour domestic growth, capex-led stocks in Samvat 2083
Domestic brokerages are tilting Samvat recommendations toward government capital expenditure plays, defence, and infrastructure over urban consumer goods. Order book execution metrics and order inflow guidance from engineering majors like Larsen & Toubro in second-quarter earnings will test this strategy. The shift reflects softening urban volume growth in fast-moving consumer goods and elevated valuations across consumer staples.
Hindu BusinessLine · +1 other
India eases forex reporting rules for small value service exports, imports
The Reserve Bank of India simplified foreign exchange documentation requirements for low-value service exports and imports. Lowering operational reporting burdens reduces administrative costs and speeds working capital cycles for mid-tier technology exporters and digital service providers. The regulatory change directly improves operating margins for smaller software exporters while streamlining cross-border remittance processing.
Reuters Business · +1 other
RBI's Rs 50,000 crore VRRR faces a muted response from the market
Banks parked ₹23,905 crore against the Reserve Bank of India's ₹50,000 crore variable rate reverse repo auction, despite system liquidity nearing ₹2 lakh crore. Lenders are retaining liquidity for upcoming festive credit demand and tax outflows rather than locking funds with the central bank. Uneven liquidity distribution across banks will keep short-term money market rates firm, supporting net interest margins for large net lenders.
ET Markets
Why mutual fund distributors are giving up multiple licences
Mutual fund distributors are consolidating multiple registration numbers into single entities following revised Securities and Exchange Board of India rules that eliminated commission-splitting tax benefits. This consolidation streamlines compliance and reporting workflows for listed asset management companies and Registrar and Transfer Agents like CAMS and KFintech. The structural cleanup reduces distributor channel friction without impacting gross equity inflows.
Mint Markets
Companies and earnings
DuPont raises annual profit forecasts, sees upbeat Q4 on healthcare, aerospace strength
DuPont raised its full-year earnings forecast on strong demand across global healthcare and aerospace end-markets. Robust aerospace and healthcare volumes signal steady export demand for Indian specialty chemical manufacturers and precision engineering suppliers servicing international supply chains. Sustained volume expansion in DuPont's advanced materials division confirms durable demand for Indian custom synthesis exporters.
Reuters Business · +1 other
NSE Q2FY27 results: Consolidated net profit rises 23% YoY to ₹2,578 crore
NSE generated a 23% year-on-year rise in Q2 consolidated net profit to ₹2,578 crore on sustained trading volumes. Management expects upcoming Sebi reforms in Securities Lending and Borrowing to expand cash market liquidity, which directly expands transaction earnings for listed market plays like BSE, CDSL, and Angel One. Q3 cash market average daily turnover will confirm this volume trajectory.
BS Markets · +1 other
Nasdaq ends higher as AI heavyweights rebound ahead of midterm results
The Nasdaq Composite rose as megacap technology stocks recovered ahead of corporate earnings and political events. US tech rallies support valuation multiples for Tier-1 Indian IT exporters by reducing risk premiums and driving foreign institutional inflows into domestic equities. Indian IT stock performance will depend on management commentary in upcoming earnings reports regarding US discretionary tech spending.
Reuters Business
Happiest Minds Q2 Results: Profit rises 15% to Rs 62 crore; revenue up 12% to Rs 645 crore
Happiest Minds reported a 15% year-on-year rise in Q2 net profit to ₹62 crore as revenue grew 12% to ₹645 crore, declaring a ₹3.05 dividend per share. Steady revenue delivery reassures mid-cap IT valuations across peers like LTIMindtree and Persistent Systems. Utilization rates and employee costs in upcoming quarter disclosures will confirm whether EBIT margins can expand further.
